source.name: transactional-outbox-relay
source.description: At-least-once async event delivery via transactional outbox: write+outbox in one transaction, relay-sweep sole retry owner, idempotent consumers, backoff+DLQ, after-commit effects. Activate wiring webhook/event delivery, an outbox, or async jobs that must not be lost/double-fired. Triggers: outbox, at-least-once, duplicate events, relay sweep."

1. **Persist + outbox in ONE transaction.** The domain write and the outbox row commit together (`DB::transaction`). Never write the outbox "best effort" after commit — a crash in between loses the event.

2. **Single retry owner = the relay sweep.** A background relay polls unsent outbox rows and delivers. The delivery job MUST NOT also `release()`/re-dispatch on failure — two owners (queue retry + relay) race on `attempts` and double-fire. Pick ONE: the relay owns retries; the job only reports success/failure.

6. **Side-effects after commit.** Broadcasts/notifications fire in an after-commit listener (`dispatchAfterCommit` / `->afterCommit()`), never inside the transaction — a rollback must not leave a sent webhook.

entries.name: transactional-outbox-relay
entries.description: At-least-once async event delivery via transactional outbox: write+outbox in one transaction, relay-sweep sole retry owner, idempotent consumers, backoff+DLQ, after-commit effects. Activate wiring webhook/event delivery, an outbox, or async jobs that must not be lost/double-fired. Triggers: outbox, at-least-once, duplicate events, relay sweep.

constraint_signals.text: description: "At-least-once async event delivery via transactional outbox: write+outbox in one transaction, relay-sweep sole retry owner, idempotent consumers, backoff+DLQ, after-commit effects. Activate wiring webhook/event delivery, an outbox, or async jobs that must not be lost/double-fired. Triggers: outbox, at-least-once, duplicate events, relay sweep."

1. **Persist + outbox in ONE transaction.** The domain write and the outbox row commit together (`DB::transaction`). Never write the outbox "best effort" after commit — a crash in between loses the event.

2. **Single retry owner = the relay sweep.** A background relay polls unsent outbox rows and delivers. The delivery job MUST NOT also `release()`/re-dispatch on failure — two owners (queue retry + relay) race on `attempts` and double-fire. Pick ONE: the relay owns retries; the job only reports success/failure.

6. **Side-effects after commit.** Broadcasts/notifications fire in an after-commit listener (`dispatchAfterCommit` / `->afterCommit()`), never inside the transaction — a rollback must not leave a sent webhook.

entries.name: transactional-outbox-relay
entries.description: At-least-once async event delivery via transactional outbox: write+outbox in one transaction, relay-sweep sole retry owner, idempotent consumers, backoff+DLQ, after-commit effects. Activate wiring webhook/event delivery, an outbox, or async jobs that must not be lost/double-fired. Triggers: outbox, at-least-once, duplicate events, relay sweep.

constraint_signals.text: description: "At-least-once async event delivery via transactional outbox: write+outbox in one transaction, relay-sweep sole retry owner, idempotent consumers, backoff+DLQ, after-commit effects. Activate wiring webhook/event delivery, an outbox, or async jobs that must not be lost/double-fired. Triggers: outbox, at-least-once, duplicate events, relay sweep."

1. **Persist + outbox in ONE transaction.** The domain write and the outbox row commit together (`DB::transaction`). Never write the outbox "best effort" after commit — a crash in between loses the event.

2. **Single retry owner = the relay sweep.** A background relay polls unsent outbox rows and delivers. The delivery job MUST NOT also `release()`/re-dispatch on failure — two owners (queue retry + relay) race on `attempts` and double-fire. Pick ONE: the relay owns retries; the job only reports success/failure.

6. **Side-effects after commit.** Broadcasts/notifications fire in an after-commit listener (`dispatchAfterCommit` / `->afterCommit()`), never inside the transaction — a rollback must not leave a sent webhook.

entries.description: Discipline for diagnosing hard bugs and performance regressions: FIRST build a tight reproducible feedback loop (that IS the skill), only then 3–5 ranked hypotheses, targeted instrumentation tagged [DEBUG-xxxx], a regression test on the right seam, cleanup. entries.name: transactional-outbox-relay
entries.description: At-least-once async event delivery via transactional outbox: write+outbox in one transaction, relay-sweep sole retry owner, idempotent consumers, backoff+DLQ, after-commit effects. Activate wiring webhook/event delivery, an outbox, or async jobs that must not be lost/double-fired. Triggers: outbox, at-least-once, duplicate events, relay sweep.

constraint_signals.text: description: "At-least-once async event delivery via transactional outbox: write+outbox in one transaction, relay-sweep sole retry owner, idempotent consumers, backoff+DLQ, after-commit effects. Activate wiring webhook/event delivery, an outbox, or async jobs that must not be lost/double-fired. Triggers: outbox, at-least-once, duplicate events, relay sweep."

1. **Persist + outbox in ONE transaction.** The domain write and the outbox row commit together (`DB::transaction`). Never write the outbox "best effort" after commit — a crash in between loses the event.

2. **Single retry owner = the relay sweep.** A background relay polls unsent outbox rows and delivers. The delivery job MUST NOT also `release()`/re-dispatch on failure — two owners (queue retry + relay) race on `attempts` and double-fire. Pick ONE: the relay owns retries; the job only reports success/failure.

6. **Side-effects after commit.** Broadcasts/notifications fire in an after-commit listener (`dispatchAfterCommit` / `->afterCommit()`), never inside the transaction — a rollback must not leave a sent webhook.

constraint_signals.text: 1. **Think Before Coding** — before editing state: what changes, why, which assumptions. On ambiguity ask ONE clarifying question, don't guess. Check: can you explain the plan in one paragraph? If not, plan isn't ready.
## Circuit Breaker — stop thresholds

- **Soft (warning):** codebase investigation >~10 tool-calls without a conclusion → stop and formulate the smallest reversible decision from current data. Ask only when a missing fact materially changes the product outcome.

- **Hard stop:** after ~20 iterations with no working result → checkpoint: describe the failed tactics, choose a genuinely different tactic or narrow the reproducer, and continue in the current root when context and capability still suffice. `session-handoff` + a new session is allowed only for a proved context/capability/owner boundary; it is not the default circuit-breaker action.
- Needs a new package or abstraction layer → ASK first.
- Second fix of the same symptom → stop, find root cause (reproduction → root cause → fix → verification), not a third patch.

- **Dependent-package boundary — ask before extending.** A dependent package (`vendor/**`, path-repo `packages/**`, shared package) is **read-only** by default. Before adding a class/provider/interface/abstraction:
within the session** — never re-issue it verbatim. The next attempt must be one of:
differing only in arguments/paths — stop, that's a repeat, not an alternative.

- **No unneeded/destructive ops.** Never `pkill`/`kill -9`/`rm` a daemon's profile, socket, or Singleton lock. Prefer the gentlest path: reuse the live process, wait for it to free up. Rebuild/restart a shared service ONLY after confirming it's idle (no live agents) — else you crash others' sessions.

entries.name: transactional-outbox-relay
entries.description: At-least-once async event delivery via transactional outbox: write+outbox in one transaction, relay-sweep sole retry owner, idempotent consumers, backoff+DLQ, after-commit effects. Activate wiring webhook/event delivery, an outbox, or async jobs that must not be lost/double-fired. Triggers: outbox, at-least-once, duplicate events, relay sweep.

constraint_signals.text: description: "At-least-once async event delivery via transactional outbox: write+outbox in one transaction, relay-sweep sole retry owner, idempotent consumers, backoff+DLQ, after-commit effects. Activate wiring webhook/event delivery, an outbox, or async jobs that must not be lost/double-fired. Triggers: outbox, at-least-once, duplicate events, relay sweep."

1. **Persist + outbox in ONE transaction.** The domain write and the outbox row commit together (`DB::transaction`). Never write the outbox "best effort" after commit — a crash in between loses the event.

2. **Single retry owner = the relay sweep.** A background relay polls unsent outbox rows and delivers. The delivery job MUST NOT also `release()`/re-dispatch on failure — two owners (queue retry + relay) race on `attempts` and double-fire. Pick ONE: the relay owns retries; the job only reports success/failure.

6. **Side-effects after commit.** Broadcasts/notifications fire in an after-commit listener (`dispatchAfterCommit` / `->afterCommit()`), never inside the transaction — a rollback must not leave a sent webhook.

constraint_signals.text: - List skills when the user asks what is available, or if the user uses this skill without specifying what to do. Default listing is `.curated`, but you can pass `--path skills/.experimental` when they ask about experimental skills.

When listing skills, output approximately as follows, depending on the context of the user's request. If they ask about experimental skills, list from `.experimental` instead of `.curated` and label the source accordingly:

- The skills at https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.system are preinstalled, so no need to help users install those. If they ask, just explain this. If they insist, you can download and overwrite.

entries.name: owner-autonomy
entries.description: Execute work autonomously and interrupt the owner only for genuine owner gates. Use for planning, implementation, audits, conflict resolution, ambiguous requests, and continuous development when routine choices can be derived from repository facts, established canons, or reversible best judgment.

constraint_signals.text: - Ask the owner only when a missing choice materially changes the product outcome and cannot be derived safely, or when explicit authority is required for an irreversible/external action.
- Do not ask for confirmation, preference, scope restatement, command selection, conflict resolution, or the next routine step when repository facts and existing canons make a safe decision possible.
- Do not ask the owner for their personal wall, room, device, or installation details unless the product is explicitly a one-off for that site.
- Stop only at a genuine owner gate, an external-state wait, exhausted authority, a safety boundary, or completed scope.

entries.name: find-skills
entries.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
